extra.message: SQL injection in the login authentication query. req.body.username and req.body.password (routes/login.js:21-22) are concatenated directly into the SQL string passed to db.one() with no parameterization or escaping. An attacker can bypass authentication entirely (e.g. username=' OR '1'='1' --) since the query is SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = '<user>' AND password ='<pass>';.

SQL injection in getProduct(). The product_id value comes from the user-controlled 'id' query parameter (routes/products.js:47, url.parse(req.url,true).query.id) and is concatenated into "SELECT * FROM products WHERE id = '" + product_id + "';". Allows UNION-based data exfiltration or boolean blind injection against the whole database.

SQL injection in search(). The 'q' query parameter (routes/products.js:67) is concatenated raw into an ILIKE pattern: "SELECT * FROM products WHERE name ILIKE '%" + query + "%' OR description ILIKE '%" + query + "%';". Injecting e.g. %' UNION SELECT ... -- allows arbitrary SQL execution.

SQL injection in purchase(). Every field inserted into the purchases table is attacker-controlled from the /products/buy request (mail, product_name, product_id, address, ship_date, phone, price - routes/products.js:100-117) and concatenated raw into the INSERT statement. A crafted request can alter the query structure or inject arbitrary SQL.

Second-order SQL injection in getPurchased(). req.session.user_name (routes/products.js:28) is concatenated into "SELECT * FROM purchases WHERE user_name = '" + username + "';". user_name originates from the raw login username (routes/login.js:30 req.session.user_name = user). After a login where the attacker-supplied name is echoed back unsanitized, it is re-injected here, so a quote/metacharacter in the session name breaks out of the string literal.

Reflected XSS. The search term 'q' from the URL (routes/products.js:67,77,83) is echoed into the page with the unescaped EJS tag <%- in_query %>. EJS <%- %> does not HTML-escape, so a payload like /products/search?q=<script>alert(document.cookie)</script> executes in the victim's browser.

Reflected XSS in the login form. The 'returnurl' query parameter is rendered with the unescaped tag <%-returnurl%> (set from url_params.returnurl at routes/login.js:12-14). An attacker can craft /login?returnurl=" onmouseover="alert(1) or inject script markup into the value attribute; because <%- %> does not escape, HTML/attribute injection and script execution are possible.

Reflected XSS. The auth_error value is rendered with the unescaped tag <%-auth_error%>. It is populated from the 'error' query parameter (routes/login.js:14 url_params.error) which itself is filled from err.message in the login redirect (routes/login.js:39). Attacker-controlled error text is injected raw into the DOM, and DB error strings can leak internal details.

Open redirect. After a successful login the server calls res.redirect(returnurl) where returnurl is taken directly from the request body (routes/login.js:23,32-36) and only defaulted to '/' when empty. Supplying returnurl=https://evil.example.com redirects the victim off-site after login, enabling phishing. The same unvalidated value is also echoed into the login page (reflected XSS / header injection surface).

cwe: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site

extra.message: CSRF / state-changing GET. The purchase action is registered with router.all('/products/buy', ...) and for GET requests reads parameters straight from the URL query string (routes/products.js:94-98). There is no CSRF token and the session cookie has no SameSite/secure hardening (app.js:43-49), so a cross-site or auto-submitted form makes an authenticated victim place an order with attacker-chosen values. Additionally the 'price' field is fully client-supplied, letting a buyer set an arbitrary price.

Security misconfiguration of the session cookie (app.js:43-49). The cookie is set with secure:false (transmitted over plain HTTP), no SameSite attribute, and a ~3.17-year maxAge. The hard-coded session signing secret (app.js:44) is also committed in source. This weakens session protection and enables cookie theft over HTTP and CSRF.

cwe: CWE-614: Sensitive Cookie in HTTPS Session Without 'Secure' Attribute

extra.message: Hard-coded credentials. Real application accounts admin/admin and roberto/asdfpiuw981 are embedded in dummy.js and seeded into the users table by model/init_db.js:24. Passwords are stored and compared in plaintext (model/auth.js:7, no hashing), and the working credentials are even printed on the public login page (views/login.ejs:26-27).

cwe: CWE-256: Plaintext Storage of a Password

extra.message: Database credentials hard-coded in source and in the connection string. The PostgreSQL user/password (postgres:postgres) are embedded for every stage (config.js:4,12,20) and the resulting connectionString (config.js:46) is built and used with no environment-variable fallback.
